summary: Suzanne Newcombe is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. She studied at Amherst College, the London School of Economics, and the University of Cambridge (PhD 2008), later holding posts at the Open University and King's College London in 2020.

Suzanne Siauve (1919–1975) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. She studied at École Normale Supérieure de Sèvres, under Louis Renou and Jacques Bacot, earning a PhD from the University of Paris (1970). She worked at CNRS and the Institut de France.

Sven Hedin (1865–1952) worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, history, archaeology, and Tibetology. He studied at Stockholm University, Uppsala University, Humboldt University of Berlin under Ferdinand von Richthofen, and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (PhD circa 1891–1892).

Sven S. Hartman (1917–1988) worked in religious studies and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Uppsala University under Henrik Samuel Nyberg, Stig Wikander, and Geo Widengren, later holding professorships at Åbo Akademi University and Lund University.

Sven Sellmer specializes in Indology, linguistics, and computational fields. He studied Indology under Horst Brinkhaus at Kiel University and has held posts at the University of Düsseldorf and Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań.
Sven Wittemann is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He earned a Master of Arts degree at the International Buddhist College, studying under his supervisor Kapila Abhayawansa (attested 2014).

Svetozar Petrović (1931–2005) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Zagreb and the University of Allahabad. He taught literature at the University of Zagreb (1959–1970), University of Novi Sad (1970–1977), and University of Belgrade (1977–1996).

Swami Japasiddhananda works in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Sri Chamarajendra Sanskrit College, Karnataka State Open University, and Visva-Bharati University (PhD 2022). He held posts at Ramakrishna Math Vivekananda Veda Vidyalaya and RKMVERI (2024).

Swami Lakshman Joo (1907–1991) was an Indology, philosophy, and religious studies scholar. He studied under Maheshwar Nath Razdan (1926–1933), taught scholars including Alexis Sanderson and Mark S. G. Dyczkowski, and founded the Universal Shaiva Fellowship in 1991.

Swami Maheshanandagiri Maharaj is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He founded the Mahesh Research Institute, founded the Advaita Grantha Ratna Manjusha (attested 1980), and served as Mahamandaleshvar Pontiff at Dakshinamurti Peetha (attested 1980).

Swami Satyananda Puri (1902–1942) worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Calcutta from circa 1924 to 1928, subsequently holding a post there from circa 1928 to 1932, and taught Somdet Phra Nyanasamvara.

Swami Shivananda (1887–1963) was a figure in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology who studied at Thanjavur Medical College. He taught Mircea Eliade and others, and he founded the Divine Life Society (1936) and the Yoga-Vedanta Forest Academy (1948).

Swami Siddheswarananda (1897–1957) was a scholar in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Madras from circa 1916 to 1920 and held a post at the Ramakrishna Order from circa 1920 to 1957.
Swami Vimalananda (1872–1908) was active in religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Ripon College and became a disciple of Swami Vivekananda in 1897.

Swami Vishnudevananda (1927–1993) was active in religious studies and Indology. He studied as a disciple under Swami Shivananda from circa 1947 to 1957 and founded the International Sivananda Yoga Vedanta Centres.

Swami Vivekananda (1863–1902) was a religious studies, philosophy, and Indology scholar. He studied at Presidency University, Scottish Church College, and the University of Calcutta, and under Ramakrishna. He taught numerous students, including Margaret Elizabeth Noble and William Hastie.

Swayam Bagaria is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He studied at Grinnell College and Johns Hopkins University (Doctorate 2020), completed a postdoctoral fellowship at the University of Virginia, and became Assistant Professor at Harvard University in 2024.

Sweta Prajapati is an Indologist who earned her PhD from Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda (1994–1997). She held the post of Director at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda in 2014 and Director in-Charge at the Oriental Institute, Vadodara (attested 2015).

Sybrandus Johannes Warren (1847–1910) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his PhD at Leiden University under Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern and served as Director of Johan de Witt-gymnasium (1879–1896) and Erasmiaans Gymnasium (1896–1910).

Sydney Frank Markham (1897–1975) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Wadham College from circa 1921 to 1924 and served as Secretary and then President of the Museums Association from circa 1929 to 1942.
